shared_elements: frontal anthropomorphic figure filling the surface
elaborate headdress or head ornament at top
circular disc / medallion at the chest
band or belt across the waist
arms bent across the torso holding a bar-like object
justification: Both are tall upright stone slabs carrying a single frontal figure organised in the same vertical register order — crowning headdress, chest disc/medallion, arms bent across a bar at the torso, waist band, and lower body below — which is a fairly specific compositional correspondence. The decisive difference is the manner of carving: A is pale stone worked in deep, densely packed high relief with intricate overlapping ornament, while B is dark, heavily eroded stone in shallow, sparse, blocky low relief with a rounded, mass-dominated silhouette.
